modern-slavery.name: Modern slavery
modern-slavery.line: I see people forced to work or marry with no way out.

sources.passage: Fifty million people were living in modern slavery in 2021, according to the latest Global Estimates of Modern Slavery.
Of these people, 28 million were in forced labour and 22 million were trapped in forced marriage.
Almost one in eight of all those in forced labour are children (3.3 million).

modern-slavery.prevalence: Fifty million people were living in modern slavery in 2021: 28 million in forced labor and 22 million in forced marriage; 3.3 million of those in forced labor are children (ILO global estimates).

tax-fairness.name: Tax fairness
tax-fairness.line: I see wealthy people and big companies pay too little in taxes.
aliases: The rich don't pay their share

sources.passage: Most Americans continue to think upper-income people pay too little in taxes.
Additionally, 70% of Americans believe corporations pay too little income tax.
the 58% holding this view is one of the lowest percentages Gallup has measured to date

tax-fairness.prevalence: 58% of U.S. adults say upper-income people pay too little in taxes and 70% say corporations pay too little (Gallup).

pay-gap.name: Pay gap
pay-gap.line: I see women still paid less than men.

sources.passage: In 2024, women earned an average of 85% of what men earned, according to a Pew Research Center analysis of median hourly earnings of both full- and part-time workers.
In 2023, full-time, year-round working women earned 83% of what their male counterparts earned, according to the Census Bureau's most recent analysis.
Nearly two-thirds of adults (64%) say women face at least some discrimination

pay-gap.prevalence: In 2024 U.S. women earned 85% of what men earned per hour (Pew); full-time, year-round women earned 83% in 2023 (Census, via Pew); 64% of adults say women face at least some discrimination (Pew).

criminal-record.name: Criminal record
criminal-record.line: My old record still keeps me out of jobs and housing.

sources.passage: 78 million people have an old legal record – one in three adults
more than half of people with an old conviction (55%) cited difficulties obtaining a job
more than 4 in 10 people with a past conviction (44%) cited difficulties obtaining housing

criminal-record.prevalence: 78 million U.S. adults, one in three, have an old legal record; 55% of people with an old conviction had trouble getting a job and 44% trouble getting housing (Alliance for Safety and Justice survey).

no-id.name: No ID
no-id.line: I don't have the ID I need to work, vote or get help.

sources.passage: Nearly 29 million voting-age U.S. citizens lacked a valid driver's license
over 7 million had no other form of non-expired government-issued photo identification

leads: Founder pool: 'i_don_t_have_the_government_issued_identification_i_need_for_ordinary_life' and four related missing-ID pains
no-id.prevalence: Nearly 29 million voting-age U.S. citizens lacked a valid driver's license, and over 7 million had no other non-expired government photo ID (University of Maryland and VoteRiders analysis).
